answer: Pin each agent to a physical place by latency triangulation: at random times, validators spread across many regions send a ping, and round-trip times reveal where the machine sits, like hearing a whisper and judging how far off the speaker stands. Two identities answering from the same knoll, within a millisecond of each other, are merged into one. A zephyr of fakes from one data center is easy to spot. To run 1,000 sybils an attacker must rent servers in 1,000 distinct locations and keep them all online.
